title: Intuit, Freshworks, and Q2 Holdings Shares Are Falling, What You Need To Know
content:
What Happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after quarterly results from two major companies raised fresh questions about AI's impact on the software sector.

IBM declined about 10% after reporting slower Q1 revenue growth, with weakness in its software business. ServiceNow also fell after noting that delayed deals in the Middle East, tied to the Iran conflict, would affect its subscription revenue growth. NOW also expects recent investments in AI to weigh on margins in the near term.

The sector-wide move reflected an ongoing debate. Some investors have questioned whether AI tools will reduce demand for traditional software or change existing license models. The results were likely read through that lens, which contributed to selling across software names beyond the two companies that reported. Though neither cause was strictly about AI suggesting the contagion was thematic not fundamental. Also, given ServiceNow was viewed as AI-resilient, its miss weakened the "safe SaaS" case, causing some analysts to lower their estimates.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 6 months ago when the stock gained 13.9% on the news that the company reported third-quarter 2025 results that exceeded Wall Street's expectations for revenue and profit and provided upbeat guidance. For the quarter, revenue grew 15.2% year-over-year to $201.7 million, beating analyst estimates.

The company's profitability also saw a significant improvement, with GAAP earnings per share of $0.23 coming in 64.3% above consensus. Adding to the positive sentiment, Q2 Holdings guided for fourth-quarter revenue slightly ahead of expectations and raised its full-year EBITDA forecast above analyst projections. This performance was underpinned by expanding profitability, as the operating margin swung to a positive 5.5% from a negative 7.3% in the prior year's quarter.

title: Freshworks Taps Kuntal Vahalia To Deepen Growth Through Partner Alliances
content:
Make better investment decisions with Simply Wall St's easy, visual tools that give you a competitive edge.

Freshworks (NasdaqGS:FRSH) appointed Kuntal Vahalia as Senior Vice President, Partnership Channel. Vahalia will lead the company’s global partner strategy, including relationships with global system integrators. The role includes a focus on expanding Freshworks’ employee experience segment across international markets.

Freshworks, known for its customer and employee engagement software, depends heavily on channel partners to reach enterprises that prefer bundled solutions and consulting support. As global system integrators gain influence in software selection and deployment, the structure and leadership of a partner program can shape how widely a platform like Freshworks is adopted.

For investors watching NasdaqGS:FRSH, this leadership change adds a new variable to how the company might pursue growth through alliances rather than only direct sales. Any impact would likely be reflected over time in the depth of partner relationships, the scale of co-selling activity and the visibility of Freshworks in large transformation projects.

Stay updated on the most important news stories for Freshworks by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio. Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Freshworks.NasdaqGS:FRSH 1-Year Stock Price Chart

Does the team leading Freshworks have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

For Freshworks, bringing in Kuntal Vahalia to run the partner channel looks like an effort to formalize how the company works with global service firms that influence large software rollouts. For you as an investor, the key angle is execution. Enterprise buyers that work with system integrators such as Accenture, Deloitte, or Infosys often prefer vendors with clear governance, incentives, and joint go to market plans. A senior leader focused on partnerships can help Freshworks present a more consistent story to those buyers, particularly for its employee experience offerings where integration with HR, IT, and security stacks matters.

How This Fits Into The Freshworks Narrative

The appointment is aligned with the existing focus on expanding the global partner program as a way to reach larger and more complex deals, supporting the push upmarket described in the narrative. If partner-led sales require higher support costs or concessions, this could challenge assumptions in the narrative about how quickly operating efficiency improves as the business scales. The specific emphasis on the employee experience segment and alliances with global system integrators is not fully spelled out in the narrative, which concentrates more broadly on AI, automation, and cloud migrations.

Story Continues

Knowing what a company is worth starts with understanding its story. Check out one of the top narratives in the Simply Wall St Community for Freshworks to help decide what it's worth to you.

The Risks and Rewards Investors Should Consider

⚠️ Execution risk if the expanded partner program adds complexity to deal cycles or creates tension between direct and partner-led sales. ⚠️ Dependence on external partners, while competitors like ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Zendesk also invest in their ecosystems, could limit differentiation if Freshworks does not keep pace on product and support. 🎁 A more mature global partner structure can help Freshworks reach larger enterprises and more geographies than its direct salesforce alone. 🎁 Stronger channel leadership may support the push into employee experience products by aligning system integrators that already advise clients on HR and IT transformations.

What To Watch Going Forward

From here, watch for concrete signs that partners are becoming a larger part of Freshworks' go to market story, such as references to co-sell activity, joint wins with major integrators, or commentary about channel contribution on future earnings calls. Also pay attention to how management describes the balance between direct and partner-led deals, and whether customers start to reference Freshworks deployments in broader transformation projects alongside bigger vendors. These details can help you gauge whether leadership changes in the partner organization are feeding through to the business in a measurable way.
